title: One audio-owner reset transaction maps the host block timeline onto graph, voice and parameter events

needles: Host timeline binding keeps four families partition invariant across resets
A refused reset leaves every family and the timeline unchanged
Binding callbacks and resets do not allocate
A graph processing failure drops its block instead of replaying it late
A block larger than the prepared graph is refused without wedging the binding

installed_sdk.rationale: host_timeline_binding.hpp is a public host header installed with the host subsystem; VoiceBankBinding gains reserve_event_reset, commit_event_reset and abort_block, and the MPE buffer gains bind_tracker_to_sink. The in-tree consumer drives the public API only.

needles: HostEventResult begin_block(const HostBlockClock& clock, HostTimelineBlock& out) noexcept;
A reset refuses old epochs and generations in every family

offline_timeline_cli.rationale: This slice adds an in-process audio-owner binding; no offline timeline command creates, drives or resets it.

offline_timeline_mcp.rationale: No MCP tool, schema or handler is added.

live_product_control.rationale: The binding is a C++ seam a graph-owning Processor drives from its process callback. No format adapter or product control drives it yet, so a musician cannot reach it through a host; this row does not claim that.

design_time_agent_manifest.rationale: Event timing and reset are runtime infrastructure, not a generator-facing capability.
